A working method for building with coding agents

A rule is only a rule when something on the disk can stop you.

design-first is a Claude Code plugin. It interviews every request before it builds, locks each decision in a manifest, builds one domain at a time and cross-checks it against all of them, and gives every rule an id and a grade that says whether a machine enforces it. A Doctor checks the disk and prints what it found, never what a document says.

89 rules in the kit. 14 stopped by a hook, 15 by a gate, 5 by nothing but the reader. The page says so because the law file says so, and this page is generated from it.

The method

Decide all of it, then build one domain at a time. The eight rules below are read from the README, so the page cannot say one thing while the kit says another. A clause id links to its grade.

The shape of it

Two ways to split a build. The left one is the thing people have been burned by: each part interviewed and built on its own, so the parts meet only at the end. The right one is what the kit does.

On one page

  1. Interview every add. A request is an opening position, not a spec: split it into decisions, give each a verdict, and ask about the real forks one question at a time. Silence is not approval.
  2. Lock decisions before code. DECISIONS.md is the one record; a later change is a Change Request, never drift. ARCHITECTURE.md is one page naming every domain and its config.
  3. Build in chunks. One domain at a time, tunable values in .json, split by subject and never by size.
  4. Cross-check every chunk against the manifest, the architecture and the goal before the next.
  5. Gate the dangerous work. Where a wrong output costs money, safety or trust, the spec gets an adversarial review before the repo exists. A review that finds nothing is a failed review.
  6. A fact about the disk is generated, never typed. Every claim a document makes about files, remotes or state is an entry in claims.json that the Doctor checks.
  7. Show nothing rather than something false. Absent is not zero, and a check that cannot look does not report green.
  8. A lesson must produce a rule. An event with no rule is a story.

A worked example

The owner says: build a tool that watches a weather feed and posts to a chat channel when the temperature crosses a threshold. The interview asks, one at a time: runtime mode (real-time, recommended), where thresholds live (a config file, recommended), what the tool must never do (never post more than N times an hour; go silent when the feed is stale, recommended). The manifest records fail-closed, the hourly cap, and that the webhook lives in an ignored secrets file. The map shows feed, rules, notify and config, one row per domain, each with its entry point and its JSON. The agent builds the feed domain first and cross-checks it (does it fail closed on a dead feed?), then rules, then notify. Six months later the owner changes the cap by editing one number in config.

The gates and the loops

The outer loop, from an idea to the next chunk. The sections below draw each part in detail. Two drawings: each loop on its own with what it costs, then the whole path with the loops on it. The dashed line is the point past which nothing runs until the decisions above it are locked.

The five loops

Each one lands on a cheaper step than the one that failed. That is what makes a wrong answer survivable.

  1. Intake sorts the owner's item by the domain test and sends it to that domain's master; the master starts the work session with a brief that names what it reports to, and the session reports to the master at turn end. (CTRL-01, CTRL-02)
  2. Interview: restate the request, give each element one verdict (approve, redact, add, flavour), rank each decision and research by its rank, and ask one question at a time with a reason on every option. Work the questions as a design tree: ask next a question whose prerequisites are settled, and find facts about the environment yourself instead of asking the owner for them. (GATE-01, OWN-04, OWN-10, GATE-15)
  3. Lock the decisions in DECISIONS.md and map the domains in ARCHITECTURE.md, with a Stack section that records each runtime, its version pin, its lockfile and its install verb. (DES-01, STACK-01)
  4. If a wrong output costs money, safety or trust, run an adversarial gap review of the spec first. In a repository that declares the gate, the guard refuses source writes until the gate is cleared. (GATE-08, GATE-09)
  5. Build the smallest slice of one chunk. (DES-05)
  6. Inner gate after each change: run the verify gate, stop, say what changed and what it proves, and wait. If it fails, go back to step 5. (GAME-12)
  7. Outer gate at the end of the chunk: cross-check against the manifest, the architecture and the goal, and check the Definition of Done; the Stop card asks once per turn. If it fails, go back to step 5. (GATE-05, GATE-07)
  8. If a locked decision must change, write a Change Request and go back to step 2. (GATE-06)
  9. Next chunk, or done.

The words, and what they are not

Most misreads of this method come from loading a familiar meaning onto one of these. Each is defined with the meaning it does not carry.

Interview
The agent interviewing the request, with the owner: split it into elements, give each a verdict, name the conflicts and the cost, then ask the real forks one question at a time. Facts about the disk are the agent's to find. stakeholder interviews. Not requirements gathering. Nothing is collected and handed to a build team.
Verdict
One of four, on every element: approve, redact, add or flavour. Silence is not approval.
Chunk
One domain, built after every decision is locked and every domain is on the map, cross-checked against the rest at its end. one department built end to end. Not a sprint. Not a time box.
Decision
One answered question in the manifest: the answer, the rationale, the date locked, what it affects, the rule for changing it. a ticket. Not a user story. Not a wish.
Manifest
DECISIONS.md. The one record, written for the next agent. a backlog. Not a spec that gets handed off and forgotten.
Design gate
The stricter pass where a wrong output costs money, safety or trust: an adversarial review of the spec before the repository exists, and a guard that refuses source writes until every finding is resolved or recorded. the ordinary case. A game does not get it.
Council
The interview for a pitch: fixed seats, each arguing one concern, then one verdict per element. a committee that decides. The owner decides; the council makes the trade-offs visible.
Owner
The one person who says yes. Nothing is locked until they say so, and nothing is built until it is locked. a product manager relaying other people's asks.
Locked
Sealed in the manifest with a date. Superseded only by a Change Request that names its successor, never edited in place.

What this method is not

  • Not vertical slices by department. Every domain is on the one-page map before the first is built, and each chunk is cross-checked against all the others.
  • Not agile sprints. A chunk is a domain and a review boundary, not a time box. No velocity, no backlog, no burndown.
  • Not big design up front and then silence. Decisions change through a Change Request that names what it supersedes, so the collision is caught in the manifest, not in the code.
  • Not a promise that a machine checks every step. Every rule is graded honestly: some are refused by a hook, some only advised, some are text that nothing checks. The grades are the chapter below the flow.

The flow

Six beats. Each one is a real recording from an install on a scratch machine, 2026-10-17, kit 0.2.0. Read down; the terminal keeps pace.

1Interview

The first command, /design-first:adopt, asks seven questions, one at a time, the recommended answer first. Silence is not approval. The command only asks; a script does every write, so the same command can undo it.

commands/adopt.md asks

  1. Root Which folder do your sessions start under? Root holds the entry CLAUDE.md and .claude/settings.json.
  2. Brain Where should your brain live? It is your private folder for personal law, claims and state.
  3. Owner name What name should the guard use for you in its messages, and the brain's me.md carry as owner.name?
  4. GitHub owner(s) Which GitHub owner(s) do your repositories push to? A remote that matches none of them is reported as FOREIGN by the Doctor.
  5. Brain as a git repo Should the brain be a git repository?
  6. Frozen paths Any frozen paths: folders the guard must refuse to edit or delete, such as a reference copy you keep on purpose?
  7. Settings scope The kit's deny/ask permission rules go in a settings file under root. Commit them or keep them personal?

2The script writes

Every file the kit writes is listed as it is written, with the reason it exists. The brain is the adopter's private layer: who they are, their own rules, their claims. Nothing about the author of the kit goes in it.

3Decide, then map

A project starts with DECISIONS.md, the one record of what was chosen and why, and ARCHITECTURE.md, one page that names every domain and its config file. A later change is a Change Request, never drift. This is the kit's own map.

ARCHITECTURE.md, core flow

law.json (+ <brain>/law.overlay.json) --> tools/law/build-law.mjs --> LAW.md (kit) / <brain>/LAW.md
                                                    ^
claims.json ------------> tools/doctor/doctor.mjs --+-- claims | survey | could-not-look --> <brain>/state/
hooks/hooks.json --------> guard.mjs / fence.mjs / ask.mjs / agent.mjs --> allow | deny | ask | rewrite | advise, + log
                           route.mjs / subagent.mjs --> LAW.md rows by group, per session, into context
                           entry.mjs --> entry path + state card (GAME-13, DES-14), into context
                           stop.mjs --> the first stop of a source turn refused once, with the card (DES-07, GATE-01/05/06/07, GAME-12)
commands/adopt.md -------> tools/adopt.mjs --> <root>/CLAUDE.md, <root>/.claude/settings*.json,
                                               <brain>/*, ~/.claude/design-first.json
commands/control.md -----> tools/control.mjs --> <brain>/control/<DOMAIN>-CONTROL.md, <brain>/control/INTAKE.md

4Build, guarded

While the agent builds, a hook reads every tool call before it runs. A force push is refused. Staging a secrets file is refused. The refusal names the rule, and the rule's grade says HOOK because this is what the grade means.

recorded 2026-10-17 - design-first 0.2.0 - hooks/guard.mjs fed two tool calls on a scratch root

$ git push --force origin main
GUARD: deny
  BLOCKED - that command destroys git history: --force rewrites published history.
 
  Git's recovery order is reflog, fsck --lost-found, stash, bundle; these commands remove exactly what that order depends on, on every branch. If this rewrite is genuinely wanted, Adopter runs it by hand.
 
$ git add .env
GUARD: deny
  BLOCKED - this command stages a file that looks like a credential: .env
 
  Secrets live in a gitignored .env, always; a token is never committed. If this one has leaked, rotate it first and assume it is already public. If this file is a deliberate exception, Adopter registers it in secretExceptions in the brain's doctor.config.json before it is staged; an exception is recorded, never assumed.

5The Doctor looks

The Doctor reads the disk, not the documents. On this fresh install every claim holds, and the survey still names what nothing has proved yet: a brain with no remote, no restore drill logged. The first recording of this beat was RED, because the new brain had no manifest; the kit now writes one, and the recording was taken again.

The parts

What is in the box, read from the box.

Hooks

Registered in hooks/hooks.json. Each runs as one Node.js process, on Windows, macOS or Linux, before or around a tool call. A hook that errors allows the call, logs it, and says so: fail loud, not fail closed.

  • PreToolUseguard.mjsEdit|Write|NotebookEdit|Bash|PowerShellrefuses the call that would stage a secret, rewrite git history, touch a frozen path, write source behind an open design gate, leave or push the loop branch, or pipe a heredoc into Python; advises on a write with no manifest or past one Read.
  • PreToolUsefence.mjsEdit|Write|Bash|PowerShellstops a deletion it can see, and an edit that removes or weakens an assertion in a measuring file, with the fence question to answer first.
  • PreToolUseask.mjsAskUserQuestionrefuses a call with more questions than the owner allows, an option with no reason, an "either is fine", or a recommended option that is not first (OWN-04).
  • PreToolUseagent.mjsAgent|mcp__ccd_session__start_sessionholds a subagent spawn, or a session start, to its brief contract, routes a subagent's model from the brain's policy, and asks past the spawn cap (DES-11, CTRL-02).
  • UserPromptSubmitroute.mjseveryinjects the law groups the prompt's words and the working folder name, once per session, plus the groups every session gets (DES-13).
  • Stopstop.mjseveryends a turn that changed source with its card, asked once: documents, the verify gate, the Change Request, the cross-check, the Definition of Done (DES-07, GATE-01, GATE-05/06/07, GAME-12).
  • SubagentStartsubagent.mjseverygives a subagent the session's law groups and the ADVISE clauses its role answers for, the ADVISE block reserved first (DES-13).
  • SessionStartentry.mjsstartupprints the brain's entry path on session start, refreshes the pointer, clears the session's routes on a compaction, and opens a repository that carries a hand-off with its state card.
  • SessionStartentry.mjsresumeprints the brain's entry path on session start, refreshes the pointer, clears the session's routes on a compaction, and opens a repository that carries a hand-off with its state card.
  • SessionStartentry.mjsclearprints the brain's entry path on session start, refreshes the pointer, clears the session's routes on a compaction, and opens a repository that carries a hand-off with its state card.
  • SessionStartentry.mjscompactprints the brain's entry path on session start, refreshes the pointer, clears the session's routes on a compaction, and opens a repository that carries a hand-off with its state card.

The law

One file, law.json, generates LAW.md. Every clause has one owning file, a verb, and a grade the generator checks against the mechanism that enforces it. A mechanism that is missing or does not declare the clause's verb and mode fails the build, and so does a hook script that hooks.json does not register.

  • SAFEProhibitions43 HOOK 1 GATE
  • PRINPrinciples43 GATE 1 OWNER
  • OWNWorking with the owner51 HOOK 4 ADVISE
  • DESDesign-first141 HOOK 1 GATE 10 ADVISE 1 BUILDABLE 1 HONOUR
  • GATEGates153 HOOK 1 GATE 11 ADVISE
  • AUTOAutonomy132 HOOK 1 GATE 3 ADVISE 1 OWNER 6 BUILDABLE
  • VCSIntegrity102 HOOK 3 GATE 1 BUILDABLE 4 HONOUR
  • OBSObservability101 GATE 4 ADVISE 5 BUILDABLE
  • GAMEGames44 ADVISE
  • DISPDisplay11 GATE
  • SKINSkins11 GATE
  • VOICEVoice11 BUILDABLE
  • MAPCanonical copies11 HOOK
  • STACKDevelopment stack31 GATE 1 ADVISE 1 BUILDABLE
  • CTRLControl31 HOOK 1 GATE 1 OWNER

The Doctor

Reads claims.json and checks each claim against the disk. Three bands: CLAIMS fail the run, SURVEY reports, COULD-NOT-LOOK is its own exit code and is never a pass. Claim types in the kit's own file:

  • config_paths_each2 in the kit's own claims
  • file_contains3 in the kit's own claims
  • file_fresh1 in the kit's own claims
  • file_not_contains1 in the kit's own claims
  • generated_matches3 in the kit's own claims
  • hook_smoke8 in the kit's own claims
  • ratchet1 in the kit's own claims
  • tree_free_of1 in the kit's own claims

Commands

  • /design-first:adoptSet up design-first on this machine. Asks seven questions one at a time, then a script writes root, brain and pointer, generates LAW.md and runs the Doctor.
  • /design-first:controlOpen a domain's master control session. Reads the domain's row from the Intake card or asks for it, renames the session, writes the control card from a template, lists and messages the domain's sessions, files them in the sidebar and pins the master. `intake` writes the Intake card.
  • /design-first:councilRun a pitch past every council seat in the project's agents folder, one question at a time, and record the verdicts. Writes the manifest only after the owner says yes.
  • /design-first:gutStress-test an idea before committing to it. Blunt devil's advocate.
  • /design-first:moveGet a recommendation (not a survey) on a decision.
  • /design-first:removeReverse what /design-first:adopt wrote. Deletes only unedited kit-written files and generated ones, keeps and lists everything you changed, removes the pointer.
  • /design-first:scopePlan a feature before building. Approach, what to reuse, simplest version, the one decision needed.
  • /design-first:shipBuild something in this codebase's style, then prove it actually works.

The reviewer

Read-only adversarial review of one change or one story against its acceptance criteria and the repo's verify gate. Use at the inner gate of a build loop, or whenever a change needs a check by something that did not write it. Returns PASS, FAIL or BLOCKED, with evidence. Never edits anything.

The grades

Pick a rule. The page shows what, if anything, stops you breaking it.

  • DENY0
  • HOOK14
  • GATE15
  • ADVISE37
  • OWNER3
  • BUILDABLE15
  • HONOUR5
gradea machine will
DENYrefuse, by a permission deny rule
HOOKinspect the call and refuse when its rule matches
ADVISEadd context, or ask once; let the call or the turn proceed
GATEstop and ask, or turn the Doctor red
BUILDABLEnothing yet: the mechanism is specified and not shipped
OWNERnothing: this is a standing ruling by the owner
HONOURnothing: this is a request
Every rule, with its grade and mechanism

Limits, stated up front

  • One adopter per user profile: one pointer, at ~/.claude/design-first.json.
  • The guard inspects tool calls. It does not see nested shells, xargs, command substitution, git aliases or scripts the agent writes; the self-test asserts these gaps.
  • The Doctor's repo survey is informational unless surveyStrict is on in your brain config.
  • The Stop card asks once per turn that changed source and grades no answer.
  • The kit never writes your user-level settings.json. When it wants a line there, it prints it.

Install

claude plugin marketplace add Jordan-Doerksen/design-first
claude plugin install design-first@design-first
/design-first:adopt

Three commands. adopt asks its questions, a script writes the files and runs the Doctor. /design-first:remove reverses exactly what adopt wrote and keeps anything you changed.
